turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the training data to identify patterns that predict high yield strength and high elongation, then match candidates to those patterns.

## Step 1: Analyze the Pareto Frontier in Training Data

From the training data, I'll identify non-dominated points (high YS AND high elongation):

Key Pareto-frontier observations:
- **High elongation (>50%) with moderate-high YS**: 
  - 206 MPa / 80% (Fe~70.6, Cr16, Ni9.5, Mo2, low C, HT1075/4h/air-cool, no aging)
  - 282 MPa / 65% (Fe~70.4, Cr16.56, Ni9.33, Mo1.74, HT1100/0.25h, aging 690°C/8000min)
  - 290 MPa / 78% (Fe~70.8, Cr16.44, Ni9.17, Mo1.6, HT1100/0.25h, no aging)
  - 278 MPa / 62% (Fe~71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1050/1h, HT2 700°C/20min)
  - 280 MPa / 64% (Fe~54.7, Cr23.5, Ni18.5, HT1180, no aging)
  - 270 MPa / 60% (Fe~68, Cr18, Ni12, HT1075)
  - 375 MPa / 53% (Fe~62.4, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5, HT1150)
  - 440 MPa / 50% (Fe~69.7, Cr21, Ni6, Mo2.15, HT1050)
  - 700 MPa / 34% (Fe~64.9, Cr11.25, Ni19.5, Ti2.9, Al0.4, HT1050, AH700°C)
  - 715 MPa / 28% (Fe~41.1, Cr15, Ni35, Ti2.8, Al1.05, HT1050, AH750°C)
  - 1000 MPa / 25% (Fe~60.5, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, Al0.4, dual AH)
  - 1300 MPa / 19% (Fe~84, Cr13, C0.2, HT1050, temper 500°C)

## Step 2: Map Candidates to Training Analogs

**c016** (Fe62.62, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5, HT1125/0.5h, no aging) — analog to 375 MPa/53% steel (same composition, slightly different HT). Expect ~350-380 MPa, ~50-55% elongation. **Strong on both axes.**

**c018** (Fe71.36, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1050/1h, HT2 700°C/20min, aging 600°C/5000min) — very close analog to 278 MPa/62% training point (same composition, same HT). Expect ~280-310 MPa, ~55-65% elongation. **High elongation, moderate YS.**

**c042** (Fe71.36, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1150/1h, HT2 500°C/10min, aging 550°C/10000min) — analog to 310 MPa/52% and 300 MPa/55% training points. Expect ~300-315 MPa, ~52-55% elongation. **Good balance.**

**c056** (Fe60.47, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, Al0.4, HT1120/4h, AH735°C/16h) — analog to 1000 MPa/25% training point (same composition, similar dual-stage AH). Expect ~900-1000 MPa, ~25% elongation. **High YS anchor.**

**c074** (Fe60.47, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, Al0.4, HT1120/3h, AH845°C/4h + AH710°C/22.5h) — similar to c056 but different AH schedule. Training analog: 620 MPa/27% (HT950, AH700°C) and 590 MPa/29% (HT1050, AH700°C). The higher solution temperature + dual AH may give ~700-800 MPa, ~28-32% elongation. **Mid-high YS with better elongation than c056.**

## Step 3: Verify Non-Domination

Estimated performance:
- c018: ~290 MPa, ~62% → high elongation anchor
- c016: ~370 MPa, ~52% → good balance
- c042: ~310 MPa, ~54% → good balance (slightly dominated by c016 potentially, but different region)
- c074: ~700 MPa, ~30% → mid-high YS
- c056: ~950 MPa, ~25% → high YS anchor

These five span the frontier well: c018 (max elongation), c016/c042 (middle), c074 (upper-middle), c056 (max YS). They are mutually non-dominated.

**Replacing c042** — checking if c051 (Fe62.37, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5, HT1100, no aging) is better: training analog is 375 MPa/53% at HT1150. At HT1100 it may be slightly lower YS but similar elongation. c016 at HT1125 is closer to the 375/53 point. Keep c042 as it fills the 300-310 MPa / 54% gap distinctly.

Final: c018, c016, c042, c074, c056
